name: Transitional Cell Carcinoma of the Corpus Uteri
aliases: Transitional Cell Carcinoma of the Endometrium

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological Diagnostic Criteria for Transitional Cell Carcinoma of the Corpus Uteri

criteria.description: Presence of malignant transitional (urothelial-like) epithelial cells in the endometrial tissue
Positive staining for urothelial markers such as uroplakin III and GATA3
Exclusion of primary transitional cell carcinoma from urinary tract or other sites by clinical and radiological evaluation
Imaging evidence of a uterine mass localized to the corpus uteri

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of transitional cell carcinoma in the corpus uteri with supportive immunohistochemical markers and exclusion of other primary sites
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of histology, immunohistochemistry, and clinical exclusion of other primary tumors.

pathognomonic.notes: Most common presenting symptom in affected women
searchTerms: unexpected bleeding from uterus in older women

pathognomonic.symptomName: Pelvic mass detected on physical examination

common.notes: Due to local tumor effect on bladder

searchTerms: low red blood cells from bleeding
anemia due to chronic blood loss

occasional.symptomName: Leg edema due to lymphatic obstruction
searchTerms: swelling in legs from lymph blockage
leg swelling due to lymph fluid buildup
numbness or weakness from brain metastases
neurological symptoms due to brain cancer spread

laboratory: Elevated serum calcium in paraneoplastic syndrome
Possible elevated tumor markers such as CA-125
imaging: Pelvic ultrasound showing endometrial thickening or mass
MRI pelvis demonstrating uterine mass with possible myometrial invasion
CT scan to assess local extension and distant metastases
genetic: No specific germline mutations identified; somatic mutations may include TP53 alterations
other: Immunohistochemical positivity for urothelial markers (uroplakin III, GATA3)

distinguishingFeatures: Glandular rather than transitional cell histology
Positive estrogen and progesterone receptor staining
More common histologic subtype of endometrial carcinoma
Primary tumor located in bladder rather than uterus
Radiologic and cystoscopic findings localize tumor to bladder

redFlags: Postmenopausal abnormal uterine bleeding persisting beyond 6 weeks
Unexplained weight loss with pelvic symptoms
references: Kurman RJ, et al. WHO Classification of Tumours of Female Reproductive Organs. 4th Edition. IARC; 2014.
Orphanet: Transitional cell carcinoma of the corpus uteri. ORPHA:213746.
